module_group_key returns a bare dotted-name string, consistent with how every module name is already represented throughout render.py/checks.py (carried-forward repo convention, not a new instance introduced by this diff).

Every new function takes exactly one parameter (module_group_key(mod), _module_line(mod), top_index(title), page_location_matches_content(m)). No growth of an existing signature in this diff (contrast g3's flagged Extractor.emit, untouched here).

The tier feature and tc31's check are each a single self-contained addition (one rewritten function + two new helpers in render.py; one new function + one CHECKS registration in checks.py). Neither required touching an ongoing pattern of call sites elsewhere.

render.py's changes are all for one axis (the top index's own two-tier structure); checks.py's one addition is for one axis (tc31's location-vs-content gap). No file mixes two unrelated reasons to change in this diff.
m.split(".") / title.split(":", 1)[0] are single split operations at their call sites, not chained navigation through multiple objects.

No unused hook, no tier-3 stub, no parameter accepted and ignored. module_group_key's own docstring states it answers 'what the prefix WOULD be for any module' so the caller can test every module against the same rule -- that generality is exercised immediately by top_index's own loop, not spare capacity for an imagined future caller.

Docstrings state design decisions and their reasoning (why tier 1 is bounded by package count not module count, what tc31's check does and does NOT prove) rather than papering over unclear naming. All new identifiers (module_group_key, _module_line, page_location_matches_content) read as exactly what they do.
